title: BDD slice C: broken variants by a different builder
item: A builder that has not opened the rule checkers writes the broken variants of the reference agent, one per rule that has a test
motivation: A slice of task 1, the BDD skill. Its content depends on what the slice before it shows.
notes: A rule with a tool-call half and a message half gets one variant per half. A variant that passes every test means that rule's checker is too weak. Each manager task gets a fresh builder, which is what keeps this builder apart from the one that wrote the checkers. Includes variants whose fault is in a message, not a tool call (says booked after no answer; reports a booking without its id; says the booking is unknown but does not ask the visitor to call): slice A's variants both made a wrong tool call. FOR THE BUILDER'S BRIEF (the advisor's condition for line 5): do not open harness/checkers.py, tests/test_slice_b.py, unchecked_sentences.json, tasks/reviews/050-1.md or tasks/advice/050-1.md, before or after writing the variants. Write each variant from rules.md and the reference agent only. This slice reports what the tests miss and fixes no checker; fixing what it finds is the next task, written from its results file. FOLDED IN (owner, 2026-11-19): run the 20 judge messages slice B wrote and did not run (judge_cases_b.json, cases J33 to J52, 2 marked hard, four new judge questions). Let probe/judge_test.py take the cases file and the result file as arguments, with today's files as the defaults, so judge_cases.json and runs/judge-test.json stay as task 56 left them. Put each message to the judge 3 times, as task 56 did (96 calls cost 0.03 USD there; this is 60). Stop at 0.50 USD and report what was spent. Use the owner's ant login, as in task 49.
done_means: (1) New broken variants written by this task's builder, each the reference agent with exactly one fault and selectable with --agent: one for each of the 10 rules a feature file cites (R-01 to R-11 without R-08), and a second for each rule whose text asks for both a tool call and a message (R-02, R-04, R-10, R-11), so each of those four has one variant with a wrong or missing tool call and one with a wrong or missing message; 14 or more in all. Three of the message variants are these: says the table is booked after a booking call with no answer (R-09), reports a booking without its confirmation id (R-05), says the booking is unknown but does not ask the visitor to call (R-11). Each variant's docstring names its rule, quotes the words of the rule it breaks and says whether the fault is a call or a message. The two variants of slice A stay unchanged and are not counted. (2) Every variant runs through all 16 feature files with 0 LLM calls, every sentence it says is a labelled entry of data.json, and the drift check, the data-file checks and the whole test suite of the café folder pass. (3) One results file lists, per variant and scenario, whether the variant's events differ from the reference agent's and the verdict of every rule; a test reruns the variants and fails when the file differs. Every variant differs from the reference agent in at least one scenario. (4) The results file gives each variant one outcome: caught (its own rule's verdict is a break in at least one scenario), caught only by another rule, or survived (every test passes). For each variant not caught it quotes the words of the rule that went unchecked and says whether unchecked_sentences.json already lists them. No variant is dropped or rewritten because it was not caught, and the branch changes neither harness/checkers.py nor unchecked_sentences.json. (5) The variants' code imports nothing from harness/checkers.py or tests/test_slice_b.py, and the builder's report lists the café files it read before it first ran the variants; harness/checkers.py, tests/test_slice_b.py and unchecked_sentences.json are not on that list. (6) probe/judge_test.py, given judge_cases_b.json, puts each of its 20 messages to the message judge 3 times and saves the result as runs/judge-test-b.json: of the 18 cases not marked hard, at least 17 are answered as expected in at least 2 of their 3 repeats; the hard cases and every case with differing repeats are listed. Run with no arguments it still reports 29 of the 29 on the saved task 56 files, which are unchanged.
draft_note: Pass lines (1) to (5) drafted by the advisor from task 050's results on 2026-11-19. Claude in chat added line (6), the brief note and outside_needs, and set priority and Ready the same day on the owner's instruction ("ready 51"). Not in this draft from the plan's outline of slice C: the clause map by script (slice B's unchecked_sentences.json is a first form of it) and the fresh reader.

decided_for_you.chosen: Advisor job d drafted done_means, verified_by, may_edit, runs_as, depends_on and tags from task 50's results, tasks/advice/051-1.md: 14 new variants (one per cited rule, a second for R-02, R-04, R-10, R-11), slice A's two not counted, survivors reported not failed, R-08 left out.
decided_for_you.rejected: Counting slice A's two variants; a variant for R-08; one variant per clause; failing the task on a surviving variant.
decided_for_you.would_change: The owner counts slice A's variants (12 new), wants R-08 in (15), wants one variant per clause, or wants a survivor to fail the task. New scope the advisor named and did not add: fixing a weak checker, the clause map and fresh reader of tasks/plans/001.md C.1 and C.2.
